analysis.objective: Build a secure customer portal, establish its GitHub repository, deploy it to Azure, validate the deployment, and diagnose and remediate deployment failures.
assumptions: The portal will be a responsive web application with authenticated customer access.
Azure and GitHub credentials, subscription details, tenant configuration, and required permissions will be provided securely.
Initial scope includes authentication, customer profile management, a dashboard, support requests, and administrator-ready APIs.
A managed Azure architecture and automated CI/CD are preferred.

proposedArchitecture.authentication: Microsoft Entra External ID or Azure AD B2C, subject to tenant availability
proposedArchitecture.hosting: Azure Static Web Apps for the frontend and Azure App Service for the API
proposedArchitecture.secrets: Azure Key Vault with managed identities
proposedArchitecture.observability: Azure Application Insights and Log Analytics
proposedArchitecture.cicd: GitHub Actions using Azure workload identity federation

coreCapabilities: Customer registration, sign-in, sign-out, and password recovery
API validation, structured error handling, and audit-friendly logging
Automated build, test, security scan, infrastructure provisioning, and deployment
constraintsAndRisks: Repository creation and deployment require authorized access to GitHub and Azure.
Identity tenant policies may affect authentication implementation.
Azure quotas, provider registration, region availability, naming conflicts, and subscription policies may block provisioning.
Production data handling, retention, compliance, and disaster recovery requirements must be confirmed before launch.
successCriteria: Application builds and automated tests pass.
Infrastructure can be provisioned reproducibly from source control.
GitHub Actions deploys without long-lived Azure credentials.
The portal is reachable over HTTPS and authenticated workflows function.
Application Insights receives logs and dependency telemetry.
Failed deployments produce an identified root cause, a documented correction, and a successful validation run.

actions: Confirm user roles, workflows, branding, accessibility, compliance, environments, and acceptance criteria.
Finalize the identity provider, domain model, API contract, and Azure region.
Create threat model, architecture diagram, and environment strategy.
Scaffold the React frontend and ASP.NET Core API.
Implement identity integration, authorization policies, dashboard, profile management, and support requests.
Add database migrations, input validation, secure headers, error handling, telemetry, and health endpoints.
Add unit, integration, accessibility, and end-to-end tests.
Create a private GitHub repository after authorization is available.
Add source code, README, contribution guidance, environment documentation, issue templates, and pull request templates.
Configure branch protection, required reviews, status checks, Dependabot, secret scanning, and code scanning.
Configure GitHub environments for development, staging, and production with appropriate approvals.
Create Bicep modules for resource groups, Static Web Apps, App Service, Azure SQL, Key Vault, Application Insights, and Log Analytics.
Configure managed identities, least-privilege RBAC, network restrictions, diagnostic settings, backups, and environment-specific parameters.
Configure GitHub-to-Azure workload identity federation.
Create pull request workflows for restore, linting, compilation, tests, dependency review, and security scanning.
Create deployment workflows for infrastructure and application components.
Deploy first to development, execute smoke and end-to-end tests, then promote through staging to production with approval gates.
Record deployment identifiers, commit SHAs, and environment URLs.
Capture the failed GitHub Actions job, Azure deployment operation details, correlation IDs, resource activity logs, and application logs.
Classify the failure as authentication, authorization, policy, quota, template, configuration, build, startup, networking, database, identity, or health-check related.
Reproduce the failure in the smallest safe scope and compare intended configuration with deployed state.
Correct the underlying source, infrastructure, permission, policy, or configuration defect rather than bypassing validation.
Add a regression test or preflight check, redeploy, run smoke tests, and document the root cause and prevention.

workstreams.name: Validation and operations
tasks: Perform failure triage and root-cause remediation when needed

buildFailure: Inspect compiler, package manager, lint, and test output.
Verify locked dependency versions and runtime SDK versions.
Reproduce with the same clean runner configuration.
Correct source or dependency issues and add regression coverage.
infrastructureFailure: Inspect Azure deployment operations and Bicep diagnostics.
Check provider registration, region support, quotas, naming rules, policy denials, and dependency ordering.
Run Bicep validation and Azure what-if before retrying.
Correct templates or subscription prerequisites and redeploy idempotently.
authenticationOrAuthorizationFailure: Validate GitHub OIDC claims, federated credential settings, tenant, subscription, and audience.
Inspect Azure role assignments and scope.
Apply only the minimum required permission and rerun the failed stage.
applicationStartupFailure: Inspect App Service logs, Application Insights exceptions, configuration, runtime stack, health probes, and database connectivity.
Verify Key Vault references and managed identity permissions.
Correct configuration or code, deploy to a slot, validate, and swap safely.
postDeploymentFailure: Run health, authentication, API, database, and browser smoke tests.
Compare application settings and schema versions across environments.
Roll back to the last known-good release if customer impact requires it, then remediate forward.
